requirement_text: Application to Bachelor's degree studies at ETH Zurich is 'in principle open to all', though applicants whose secondary-school diploma is not directly recognized for admission must pass an ETH entrance examination before commencing studies. ETH determines individually, only after receiving the applicant's complete application in eApply, whether an entrance exam is required at all, and if so whether it is the reduced or comprehensive version — an applicant cannot reliably self-determine this in advance.
source_authority_note: ethz.ch is ETH Zurich's official domain; not .edu/.ac./.gov.
researcher_notes: This is ETH's OWN institution-specific entrance exam, distinct from the ECUS exam used by other Swiss universities and distinct from EPFL's CMS/entrance exam — see Switzerland-system file record REQ-2026-08-21-0011 for how the national matrix groups ETH and EPFL as an analogous-but-separate 'special tier'.

requirement_text: Reduced entrance examination: covers 4 examination subjects, fee CHF 550. Applies 'in most cases' where the applicant holds a degree 'very similar to, but not equivalent to a Swiss Matura.'
limitations: The exact list of the 4 examined subjects was not extracted in this research pass — ETH's page references a downloadable subject-list PDF that was not independently fetched. Recommend a follow-up fetch of that PDF before treating subject specifics as final.
researcher_notes: Genuine entrance-exam pathway shape — not converted into a fake numeric score threshold.

requirement_text: Comprehensive entrance examination: covers 8 examination subjects, fee CHF 800. Required 'if your educational background is only partially equivalent to the Swiss Matura (fewer subjects or lower level), or if you do not have a Matura or a similar qualification.'
limitations: Exact list of the 8 subjects not extracted in this pass; ETH's page defers to a downloadable PDF not independently fetched.

requirement_text: The ETH entrance examination itself is conducted in German: 'The examination is in German. Familiarity with the respective subject terminology in German is a prerequisite.' The exam covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, history, geography, and languages (German, English, French, Italian). Notably, 'there are no subject area lists for mathematics, physics and chemistry' — i.e. no fixed published syllabus for those three subjects, unlike some other subjects which do have published materials/literature lists.
researcher_notes: The 'no fixed subject-area list for math/physics/chemistry' point is genuinely notable and easy to lose — recorded explicitly so it isn't flattened into 'standard syllabus applies.'

requirement_text: 'The main teaching language in all Bachelor's degree programmes is German.' Applicants must meet German language proficiency standards as part of the general (non-exam) application; a German language certificate may be required, and 'applications with invalid, insufficient or missing language certificates will be rejected after 31 March on formal grounds.'
limitations: requirement_category_db uses 'english_proficiency' loosely here per the closest available enum match — this is actually a GERMAN-proficiency requirement, not English. Flagging explicitly since the enum's literal name is misleading for this record; 'language_proficiency' would be a better fit if available in the actual production enum.
researcher_notes: IMPORTANT for ORYN: ETH's teaching language is German, not English, for Bachelor's programmes — a common misconception given ETH's international reputation for English-medium research/graduate work.

requirement_text: 'You may apply for one Bachelor's degree programme only' and 'At ETH Zurich it is only possible to start Bachelor's degree studies in the Autumn Semester' — there is no spring-semester Bachelor's intake.

ETH Zurich's Bachelor in Human Medicine requires the EMS: 'a central test' used to 'determine the applicant's aptitude for medical studies' at ETH Zurich, Zurich, Bern, Fribourg, and Basel universities. Application is via the swissuniversities online platform ('Application via swissuniversities is mandatory'). Due to the limited number of places, 'particular admission regulations apply' — i.e. a numerus clausus.

Human Medicine at ETH Zurich has citizenship/residency restrictions not present in ETH's other Bachelor programmes. Eligible categories include: Swiss citizens/Liechtenstein citizens; non-Swiss holders of Swiss settlement (C) permits; non-Swiss individuals married to Swiss citizens meeting specific criteria; EU/EFTA citizens employed in medical professions in Switzerland for a minimum of 1 year; and recognized refugees. General domicile definitions from Swiss Civil Code Article 23 apply. This program 'operates under [a] separate ordinance specifically governing restrictions on admission to the BSc programme in Human Medicine.'
limitations: Exact statutory citation for the 'separate ordinance' was not independently pulled and verified in full text during this pass.
researcher_notes: Consistent with (not conflicting with) the general Switzerland-wide EMS citizenship/residence restriction recorded in the system file (REQ-2026-08-21-0007) — ETH's page gives the more granular eligible-category breakdown.

requirement_text: Required application documents for non-Swiss-matriculation applicants include: passport photo, valid ID copy, curriculum vitae, upper secondary school-leaving certificate, school reports from the final three years, a German language certificate (if required), and a signed declaration of consent. Processing 'can take up to eight weeks' after submission.
